subject: Re: Econ fit surface and staged onramp plan
messages:
From: Marina Solis <marina.solis@brightlayer.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com
Date: 2026-07-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — cost parity options and migration safety plan

Hi Soojin / Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the performance looked strong. Procurement asked me to get a short summary of what Redwood can offer to match our incumbent economics and how you’d stage a migration so we don’t regress on latency or run costs. Key questions:
- Can you map the effective $/1M tokens and call out where committed capacity vs. burst affects price?
- What one-time credits or migration waivers are available (eg. egress, pilot credits, professional services)?
- We need a rollback/escape-hatch plan in case the first-month latency SLOs miss by >10%.

I attached our RFI + SOW for context. Procurement would like a response by EOD next Tuesday if possible.

—Marina
BrightLayer — Director, Cloud Procurement

Attachment: BrightLayer_RFI_SOW.pdf

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Marina Solis <marina.solis@brightlayer.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — cost parity options and migration safety plan

Marina — thanks for the clear asks. High level reply below; I’ll attach a short econ worksheet and a staged onramp we recommend.

1) Effective economics
- Hosted API baseline: $0.018 / 1k tokens for standard generation workloads; embeddings at $0.005 / 1k units.
- Committed Dedicated: we can reach an effective $/1M tokens ~35–45% lower depending on commit length and batch profiles.
- Burst pricing: 20% premium over committed if you exceed burst buffers; we recommend a conservative burst cap in the first 30 days.

2) One-time concessions we can offer for a first-year pilot
- $150k pilot credit (applied to hosted + Dedicated on first invoice)
- Waived egress fees for first 90 days for the initial migration transfer (standard T&Cs apply)
- One discounted day of on-site / remote PS for integration and KV cache tuning (up to 8 hours)

3) Rollback / escape hatch
- Canary rollout by region with traffic split and automated fallback to incumbent model endpoints if 95th p99 latency > target for 3 consecutive hours.
- Daily latency and quality checks; if thresholds fail we’ll execute a fast rollback plan (DNS-weighted routing and retained cached model shards) — typically a 1–3 hour mitigation window.

I’ve attached redwood_quote_BL-5421.xlsx and a draft migration_runbook_v1.2.pdf. Aditya — can you add a quick note on the KV/caching operational assumptions? Laura — flagging for approval on the pilot package (credit + egress waiver).

Best,
Soojin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_quote_BL-5421.xlsx, migration_runbook_v1.2.pdf

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, Marina Solis <marina.solis@brightlayer.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — technical assumptions and rollback details

Marina / team — adding technical color so procurement can validate risk: 

- KV cache warming: for chat-heavy flows we recommend a 48–72 hour warm window against production traffic in a shadow capacity. Expect initial token cost uptick (~8–12%) while cache fills; this is covered by the pilot credit.
- Quantization profile: we’ll serve the pilot on int8 variants (verified perf profile) unless you require FP16 for certain prompts — we can toggle per-model. Int8 gives ~1.6x throughput on our Dedicated nodes.
- Rollback specifics:
  * Retain incumbent routing for 14 days as a standby.
  * We’ll push observability hooks (trace ids, token-level latency) into your telemetry; if p99 degrades we switch traffic weight to incumbent in 15-minute increments until stable.

Operational ask: we need a named contact for SRE coordination and a list of critical prompts you want in the first-week eval set.

—Aditya
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, Marina Solis <marina.solis@brightlayer.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — approval and adjusted concession framing

Marina — I’ve reviewed the ask and can approve the pilot package with a small tweak: 

- Pilot credit increased to $180k (covers cache warm and initial burst)
- Egress waiver remains 90 days, but instead of a full waiver we’ll cap egress exposure at $20k then review usage — this keeps risk mutualized.
- We’ll include two 4-hour PS blocks focused on KV tuning and latency SLO validation (remote).

Please confirm you can accept those terms and we’ll prepare a short Addendum to the MSA. Soojin — please draft the addendum and update the DocuSign flow. Aditya — include the required SRE contact list in the runbook.

—Laura
VP, North America Sales

From: Marina Solis <marina.solis@brightlayer.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com, laura_bennett@brightlayer.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — confirmation and next steps

Thanks — the updated terms are acceptable. We appreciate increasing the pilot credit and the shared egress cap; that addresses procurement’s primary concerns. Two quick items before legal signs: 
- Please send the addendum + quote as a consolidated DocuSign.
- SRE contact for cutover: Jordan Miles (jordan.miles@brightlayer.com) — we’ll share the eval prompt set by Monday.

If you can circulate the DocuSign by EOD Friday we’ll aim to have legal and procurement complete the review next week.

Best,
Marina
BrightLayer — Director, Cloud Procurement
